paper.title: March in Chat: Interactive Prompting for Remote Embodied Referring Expression
paper.central_claim: MiC lets a REVERIE agent talk to an LLM on the fly: Goal-Oriented Static Planning (GOSP) names the target object and its likely room, a CLIP-based Room-and-Object Aware Scene Perceiver (ROASP) describes the current room and visible objects, and Scene-Oriented Dynamic Planning (SODP) regenerates step-by-step instructions on room change with retrieved demonstrations; the assembled instruction guides a pretrained HM3D-DUET agent and outperforms the previous state of the art by large margins on SPL and RGSPL.

signatures.object: Interactive instruction generation for a pretrained REVERIE navigation agent: LLM writes goal and step plans, perceiver feeds back room/object text.
signatures.information: High-level instruction; ROASP text ('I am in <room>, I can see <objects>' top-3 objects from a closed label set); retrieved FGR2R demonstration; previous steps.
signatures.operation: GOSP once (target + likely room) -> at each step ROASP -> if predicted room changed, SODP prompts the LLM for the next step instruction and appends it -> agent consumes [HLI, GOSP, SODP] tokens.
signatures.output: Text instruction W=[W_I, W_G, W_S] for the HM3D-DUET agent.
signatures.conditions: REVERIE panoramas in Matterport3D; GPT-2 in-context learning; room label vocabulary from MP3D annotations.
signatures.feedback: Room-type change detected by CLIP triggers re-planning.
signatures.selection_rule: Nearest-neighbor demonstration by Sentence-BERT cosine similarity; no verifier on LLM output.
signatures.persistence: Instruction text accumulates within an episode.
signatures.later_use: Re-read by the agent each step; no cross-episode state.
signatures.claimed_effect: Test unseen SPL 41.97 vs 38.88 (HM3D-DUET), RGSPL 26.17 vs 22.68; val unseen SPL 43.60 vs 40.49.
signatures.failure_boundary: Plan relevancy/rationality 2.06/1.93 of 3; closed vocabulary; room-change trigger only.

gap.author_gap: REVERIE gives only short high-level instructions; prior LLM planners handle atomic manipulation in small scenes and are static, so large multi-room environments need an environment-aware LLM planner.
gap.checked_gap: A real difficulty (high-level instructions) and a named neighbor class, but the premise that LLM world knowledge is the missing ingredient is not isolated from extra text conditioning, and the strongest LLM-planning neighbor is not run.
lineage: LLM planners: Huang et al. 2022, SayCan, Inner Monologue, Song et al. (concurrent, ALFRED)

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Closed-loop simulator-judged navigation on the standard REVERIE splits; no real robot or unused embodiment.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: With GPT-2 in-context text plans and CLIP room/object feedback fed to a pretrained HM3D-DUET agent, REVERIE test-unseen SPL/RGSPL rise by about 3.1/3.5 points in a single run; component toggles on val unseen are ordered consistently.
assessment.cannot_claim: 'Large margins', that LLM world knowledge (rather than extra conditioning text) causes the gain, robustness to seeds, any cost viability, generality beyond REVERIE.

G.reason: Genuine difficulty (high-level instructions in large multi-room environments) and cited LLM-planner neighbors, but the nearest LLM-planning neighbor is not run on REVERIE and the residual after the method (large human gap) is not characterized.

M.reason: Goal reasoning, room-aware replanning and retrieved demonstrations form a coherent response with partial ablations; mechanism by which a trained agent exploits the text and the LLM identity/training use are unclear.

X.reason: Main modules and trigger are described, but demonstration retrieval hyperparameters, how generated instructions enter agent training, max steps, prompt text (figure-only) and baseline details (supplement) are missing; limitations are not discussed.

measurement.reason: Standard simulator-computed SR/SPL/RGS metrics with a defined 3 m success radius, but single run per configuration, per-split episode counts not stated, and results come from one pretrained agent.

causality.reason: One-at-a-time GOSP/SODP/ROASP toggles exist, but no control gives the agent the same room/object text without the LLM, no second backbone, no seeds, and dynamic-demonstration value is shown only by human ratings.

evidence.quote: Our MiC model outperforms the previous state-of-the-art by large margins by SPL and RGSPL metrics on the REVERIE benchmark.
evidence.support_explanation: Author headline claim; test-unseen gains are +3.09 SPL and +3.49 RGSPL in single runs.

evidence.quote: For the LLMs, we use the public GPT-2 [ 31 ] model for in-context learning.
evidence.support_explanation: The only statement of the LLM identity: GPT-2, not a frontier model; plausibility against the plans shown in Fig 6 is doubtful but unverifiable here.

evidence.quote: However, previous works mainly utilize LLMs to plan atomic actions of object manipulation in a very limited space with simple scenes.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: LLM planners not explored for large REVERIE environments.

evidence.quote: These two LLM planners are static, which only generate action plans at the beginning of a task.
evidence.support_explanation: Author characterization of prior LLM planners; Song et al. (concurrent) is described but not compared.

evidence.quote: we choose the training set of the Fine-Grained R2R dataset (FGR2R) [ 15 ] as the demonstration set
evidence.support_explanation: Retrieval bank for dynamic demonstrations.

evidence.quote: both of which are embedded by the Sentence-BERT [ 32 ]
evidence.support_explanation: Demonstration retrieval by cosine similarity.

evidence.quote: we use CLIP [ 30 ] as the proposed room-and-object aware scene perceiver
evidence.support_explanation: ROASP is CLIP zero-shot classification over closed room/object label sets.

evidence.quote: the room type labels from the MatterPort3D [ 6 ] semantic annotations
evidence.support_explanation: Room-label vocabulary taken from Matterport3D annotations (closed vocabulary).
